_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); machinery and engines signals

pit_profile.why: 'Caterpillar Inc. is shaping the future as the world’s leading manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, off-highway diesel and natural gas engines, industrial gas turbines and diesel-electric locomotives' (FY2025 10-K, Item 1); 'Caterpillar products and services are sold worldwide into a variety of highly competitive markets'; 'The demand for our products and services tends to be cyclical and can be significantly reduced in periods of economic weakness characterized by lower levels of government and business investment, lower levels of business confidence, lower corporate earnings, high real interest rates, lower credit activity or tighter credit conditions, perceived or actual industry overcapacity, higher unemployment and lower consumer spending.', 'The energy and mining industries are major users of our products, including the mineral extraction, oil and natural gas industries.' and 'Changes in environmental and climate change laws or regulations, including laws relating to greenhouse gas emissions, could lead to new or additional investment in product designs and could increase environmental compliance expenditures.' (Item 1A): the 10-K calls the demand for its own products cyclical (BKR's 'Our business is cyclical'), so CYCLICAL from the FY2010 10-K; ENERGY_TRANSITION (live from 2015-12-12) is scoped to oil, gas and coal reserves and refining, which a maker of construction and mining equipment, engines and turbines does not hold, and EV (live from 2020-01-01) to battery-electric vehicles displacing ICE powertrains, auto parts suppliers and fuel retail, which its machines, off-highway engines and turbines are not, so the climate-change wording stays here

classification.quality_note: 'Caterpillar Inc. is shaping the future as the world’s leading manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, off-highway diesel and natural gas engines, industrial gas turbines and diesel-electric locomotives' (FY2025 10-K, Item 1); 'Caterpillar products and services are sold worldwide into a variety of highly competitive markets'; 'The demand for our products and services tends to be cyclical and can be significantly reduced in periods of economic weakness characterized by lower levels of government and business investment, lower levels of business confidence, lower corporate earnings, high real interest rates, lower credit activity or tighter credit conditions, perceived or actual industry overcapacity, higher unemployment and lower consumer spending.', 'The energy and mining industries are major users of our products, including the mineral extraction, oil and natural gas industries.' and 'Changes in environmental and climate change laws or regulations, including laws relating to greenhouse gas emissions, could lead to new or additional investment in product designs and could increase environmental compliance expenditures.' (Item 1A): the 10-K calls the demand for its own products cyclical (BKR's 'Our business is cyclical'), so CYCLICAL from the FY2010 10-K; ENERGY_TRANSITION (live from 2015-12-12) is scoped to oil, gas and coal reserves and refining, which a maker of construction and mining equipment, engines and turbines does not hold, and EV (live from 2020-01-01) to battery-electric vehicles displacing ICE powertrains, auto parts suppliers and fuel retail, which its machines, off-highway engines and turbines are not, so the climate-change wording stays here. cyclical (obsolescence risk 2/5); price rich; +298% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap -1.11; conservative 2yr -52%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -42.5%/yr (worst year FY16-FY25, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +24.6%/yr (Q1 sales and revenues + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +24.6%/yr (FY16-FY25 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +81.1%/yr (best 2-yr run FY16-FY25); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: CAT (retrospective, 2026-06-18) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B infx (92.6% downside to Bear $73 / +-38.7% upside to Bull $604) | Adj composite 2.50 vs market 3.61: gap -1.11 [OVERVALUED] | +298% above the EPP floor $248 (13x FY26E $19.06) | Conservative 2-yr case: -52.1% total (-26.1%/yr) | At 51.7x FY26E the 15% hurdle price $1,304 sits above the BULL case; Machinery sales +23.8% in Q1 2026, forward revenues +22.2% (no FY26 sales and revenues guide in numbers, Q1 2026 growth); ENERGY_TRANSITION (live from 2015-12-12) and EV (live from 2020-01-01) are scoped to oil, gas and coal reserves and refining and to battery-electric vehicles; no theme in scope has dated evidence.
